title: Sample 17-14: Errors to be Identified in Exercise

illustrates.quote: Marked Spelling Errors. When print calls attention to errors by means of a font attribute (e.g., underline, italics, color, highlighting, etc.) the designated words are uncontracted, and the remainder of the passage is contracted.

blocks.text: Write the letter of the answer that correctly respells each underlined word. If the word is correct, write D.
Anton (a) `believes` that (b) `coperation` is possible, and he thinks that peace is an (c) `achieveable` goal.

resolution: Both runs (A, B) came from the same model (Gemini Pro via Antigravity, 17 Sep 2026) and are not independent; agreement was treated as no evidence. braille.lines independently re-extracted from references/_text/braille-formats-2016.txt (the line-number field, digits + >=3 spaces, or the fixed left margin measured in ASCII spaces before any U+2800 cell, stripped by counting; U+2800->space; trailing spaces removed). Braille and rule id unchanged (both agreed '17.10.3'). The print numeral-beneath-word convention is re-expressed here as an inline '(a)'/'(b)'/'(c)' marker directly in the sentence text (Emboss has no positioned-beneath-word annotation mechanism at all, and the given braille itself uses its OWN devised bracketed marker '<#a>' rather than reproducing the print numeral literally, so there is no existing segment type this reconciliation could target for a match); the answer-key grid (only item 'a' fully given, 'b' abridged with '444') is recorded as 'other', not modeled.
